stem:
Esha has a square rangoli tile with a design on it. She wants to know whether the design has mathematical symmetry.

Which two claims are correct?

options.text: A fold that maps the design onto itself shows symmetry.
Matching colours alone settle that the design is symmetric.
A turn that maps the design onto itself shows symmetry.
A definite pattern of matching parts is what creates symmetry by itself.

teacher.key_rationale: Mathematical symmetry is decided by a fold or turn that maps the design onto itself. Colour match alone omits the transformation. Claiming matching parts create symmetry reverses the relation.
